title: Prefix cache sensitivity sweep and operational metrics suite
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Create a reproducible benchmark suite that sweeps prefix/KV cache configurations across hit rate, memory budget, concurrency and sequence-length distributions to produce operational curves (tokens/sec vs p95 vs memory). Integrate statistical regression detection and automated alerts so any runtime change that meaningfully degrades observed p95 or throughput surfaces as a regression ticket with artifacts.
background: We've observed occasional regressions after kernel selection and batching changes where average tokens/sec is unchanged but tail latency (p95/p99) and memory usage regress. Existing harnesses test single workloads or fixed hit rates. This ticket builds a multi-dimensional sweep harness and a reproducible analysis pipeline that produces operational curves used in code review and can be run nightly against head and baseline builds.
goals: Implement an extensible harness that runs sweeps over hit_rate=[0,10,25,50,75,90]%, memory_budget=[256MB,512MB,1GB], concurrency=[1,8,32,128], seq_len=[64,512,2048,8192]
Collect tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99, CPU/GPU utilization, process RSS, KV cache hits/sec, cache-eviction rate, batching stats, and read amplification for each cell
Produce operational-curves (tokens/sec vs p95) and heatmaps for hit-rate vs p95 vs memory
Integrate regression detection comparing baseline runtime-1.18 to candidate runtime-1.19 using CUSUM + bootstrap CI with configurable thresholds
Auto-upload artifacts to GS and update Grafana dashboards and create Linear regression tickets when thresholds breached
success_metrics: Harness runs end-to-end with >95% successful sample collection for the full sweep within 6 hours
Regression detector has <5% false positive rate on historical backtest over last 6 months of commits
New baseline operational curves committed and surfaced in PRs for all runtime perf changes
test_plan: Phase 1: Minimal runnable harness for single model and single seq_len to validate instrumentation (tokens/sec, latency, rss)
Phase 2: Expand to full hit-rate x memory x concurrency x seq_len grid and add batching-window knobs (1ms..50ms)
Phase 3: Run nightly head vs baseline comparisons and backtest detector against historical traces
Phase 4: Integrate alerting to create Linear tickets and post summary to #infra-perf-channel with links
benchmarks_to_run: Workload MultiTurn: alternating prefixes of 64/512; simulates repeated prefix hits to stress KV reuse
Workload TailStress: high concurrency with large seq_len to expose eviction pressure
measurement_details: Tokens/sec computed over completed token-generations excluding retries
Latency measured at request-level and token-level; report p50/p95/p99 request latencies
Memory measured as peak RSS per worker and aggregated cache memory accounting
Cache hit rate computed at prefix-key granularity and also as per-request hit fraction
Batching: record avg batch size, batch wait time distribution, and batch composition heterogeneity
regression_detection: Detector: CUSUM for persistent shifts + bootstrap to compute 95% CI for p95 and tokens/sec
Primary thresholds: p95 increase >10% AND absolute p95 increase >20ms OR tokens/sec drop >8% triggers investigation
Secondary checks: check p99 and batch composition changes to avoid false positives due to workload skew
Backtesting: run detector over last 100 commits to compute false positive/negative rates and tune alpha
artifacts_and_outputs: Normalized operational curve images (PNG) and interactive Grafana panels
Compressed raw traces (tanon logs) stored at gs://redwood-bench/prefix-sweeps/ENG-26209/<run-id>/
Regression report with CIs and delta tables uploaded to runtime PRs
integration_points: CI: add nightly job runtime/perf/prefix-sweep in Jenkins
Dashboards: grafana.com/redwood/perf/prefixcache (panel IDs will be added in PR)
GitHub: runtime repo PR template will include link to latest operational curves (example PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/987)
Alerts: post to #infra-alerts and create Linear ticket template with run artifacts
risk_mitigation: Large sweep time: allow partial-run resume and prioritized sweep cells to surface high-risk regions faster
Noisy traces: add deterministic traffic replay mode with seedable workload generator
Resource cost: cap concurrent sweep runs and use dedicated bench cluster to avoid impacting prod
False positives: require multi-metric confirmation (p95 + tokens/sec or p99 + eviction spike) before auto-creating P0 tickets
notes: We intentionally include both per-request and per-token latencies because changes to batching can hide token-level regressions
Cache accounting needs patch in runtime to export 'cache_bytes_allocated' and 'per_key_entry_count' — see ENG-27011 (follow-up)
Consider adding synthetic 'hot-prefix' microbenchmarks for kernel-level analysis if we see unexplained p95 spikes
